key_insight: Tree-based machine learning models can accurately predict halide perovskite band gaps from simple atomic and structural descriptors, revealing that B-site and X-site chemistry drives much of the variation.
engineering_relevance: These models can accelerate screening of lead-free perovskites by narrowing the search for compositions with target band gaps for optoelectronic and solar-cell applications.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regressors on atomic and structural features across multiple halide perovskite families.
Compared random forest regression, gradient boosted regression trees, and XGBoost for band-gap prediction.
Used feature importance analysis to identify the most influential descriptors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy from RFR, GBRT, and XGB across various halide perovskite compositions, supported by feature-importance analysis.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and diversity of the training dataset, so extrapolation to unfamiliar compositions or structures should be treated cautiously.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
